title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
spaceBreakdown:
- queue<TreeNode*> q: up to n/2 entries (widest level of a balanced tree) → O(n)
- vector<int> level: up to n/2 entries, moved into result → part of output, not counted
- not counted: result (returned output), input tree
approach: Use breadth-first search with a queue, processing one tree level per iteration. Before popping any nodes, record the current queue size - this gives the exact count of nodes at the current depth. Pop exactly that many nodes, collect their values, and enqueue their children. This groups nodes by depth and preserves left-to-right order within each level.
hints: What property is shared by every node that ends up in the same inner list? The tree can have up to 2000 nodes.
Use a queue for breadth-first traversal. For root [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]: enqueue 3, record queue size (1), pop exactly 1 node, enqueue its children 9 and 20 - that completes level 0.

```
q = new queue
q.push(root)
while q not empty:
    sz = q.size()
    level = []
    for i in 0..sz-1:
        node = q.pop()
        level.append(node.val)
        if node.left: q.push(node.left)
        if node.right: q.push(node.right)
    result.append(level)
return result
```

**Empty tree** - root is null, the only valid empty input
`Input: []` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: pushing root to queue without a null check, then accessing `node->val` on nullptr → undefined behavior, crash

**Not saving level size** - the queue grows as children are enqueued during iteration
`Input: [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]` → `Expected: [[3],[9,20],[15,7]]`
⚠️ Bug: writing `for (int i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)` instead of saving `int sz = q.size()` first → processes children in the same level, returns `[[3,9],[20,15],[7]]`

**Skewed tree** - every node has at most one child, forming a chain of depth n
`Input: [1,2,null,3,null,4,null]` → `Expected: [[1],[2],[3],[4]]`
⚠️ Bug: using recursive DFS with `result[depth].push_back(val)` without first ensuring `result.size() > depth` → out-of-bounds access, crash

**All-equal values** - every node has the same value
`Input: [7,7,7,7]` → `Expected: [[7],[7,7],[7]]`
⚠️ Bug: using a `set<int>` to deduplicate values within each level → returns `[[7],[7],[7]]`, dropping duplicate values

followUps.q: Return the level order traversal from bottom to top (LeetCode 107).
followUps.a: Run the same BFS and reverse the result vector before returning. TC stays O(n), SC stays O(n).

followUps.q: Return a zigzag traversal where odd levels go right-to-left (LeetCode 103).
followUps.a: Track a boolean flag that flips each level. When the flag indicates reverse order, reverse the level vector before appending. TC stays O(n), SC stays O(n).

followUps.q: The tree is too large to store all levels in memory at once - return one level at a time as a stream.
followUps.a: The queue already holds only one level at a time. Yield each level vector as soon as it is built, then discard it. TC stays O(n), SC drops to O(w) where w is the maximum width of the tree.
